findings.evidence: features/008-optimize-skill/008-optimize-skill-prd.md:R11 + AC-10 — R11 introduces score-direction handling: 'The target\'s `eval:` field declares whether its primary score is `direction: maximize` (e.g. `simplify`\'s lines deleted) or `direction: minimize` (e.g. `feedback-loop-audit`\'s CONTEXT.md length). Targets without a declared direction default to `maximize`.' AC-10 verifies the direction-aware winner-pick rule: 'For a target whose `eval:` declares `direction: maximize` ... the winner-pick rule selects the highest-score variant. For a target whose `eval:` declares `direction: minimize` ... the winner-pick rule selects the lowest-score variant.' But the existing target SKILL.md `eval:` fields (per `skills/simplify/SKILL.md` line 11 and `skills/feedback-loop-audit/SKILL.md` line 11) are SINGLE STRINGS — free-form prose describing the eval clauses. There is no structured shape for declaring `direction:` as a sub-field. R11 commits to a `direction:` declaration mechanism that no R-level requirement establishes — the eval-frontmatter shape is locked-in architecturally as a string, and changing it to a structured field is a Phase 1 cross-skill schema change implicit in this Phase 3 PRD. AC-10 verifies a contract that no R defines: where does the `direction:` live? In the eval string itself? As a parallel `eval_direction:` frontmatter key? In an extended structured eval field?
findings.claim: Coverage gap (orphan AC) — AC-10 verifies a `direction: maximize | minimize` declaration mechanism that no R-level requirement establishes. Goal-Driven Execution principle: 'Every requirement is covered by at least one AC. The inverse also holds: every AC must verify at least one stated requirement, otherwise the AC is testing a contract the PRD didn\'t make.' R11 names the direction-handling rule but does not define WHERE in the target SKILL.md the direction is declared, leaving AC-10 verifying a contract whose mechanism is unstated. Additionally — and this is the load-bearing concern — implementing the mechanism almost certainly requires extending the `eval:` frontmatter shape across every existing target skill (`simplify/SKILL.md`, `feedback-loop-audit/SKILL.md`, etc.), which is Phase 1 cross-skill schema creep smuggled into a Phase 3 PRD body.
findings.proposed_change: Add a new requirement R17 that explicitly defines the direction-declaration mechanism AND the cross-skill schema dependency: 'R17. Score-direction declaration. The target SKILL.md\'s `eval:` field is augmented with a structured score declaration of the form `score: { signal: "{description}", direction: "maximize|minimize" }` placed alongside the existing free-form eval prose. Targets without the structured score block default to `direction: maximize`. R17 requires extending every initial-six target skill\'s SKILL.md with the structured score block before `/optimize` v1 can run on them; this is a cross-skill schema dependency and ships via separate per-target `simplify`-style enhancement PRDs (one per target) before `/optimize` v1 lands. Trace: interview Round 2 + Gate 2 review goal-r1-f1 — winner-pick rule needs explicit score-direction handling. Serves goal: Outcome (the same loop works for both maximize and minimize surfaces).' Then update AC-10\'s `Verifies:` line to cite R17 specifically. This closes the orphan-AC gap AND makes the cross-skill schema dependency explicit (rather than burying it inside R11).

findings.evidence: features/008-optimize-skill/008-optimize-skill-prd.md:Goal Outcome + Users (tertiary) + AC-1 through AC-15 — The goal\'s Outcome and Users sections name 'Phase 3 self-learning consumers (`/insights`, `/prune`) mine `optimize-runs.jsonl` for which targets converge, which keep failing variants, which the human always rejects (a signal the eval is missing something).' AC-15 verifies the run-record schema (which fields are present), but no AC verifies that the corpus is *mineable* — specifically that (a) the `id` field is unique across records (so a Phase 3 consumer can join records without ambiguity), (b) the `winner_operator` field is preserved on declined records (so the operator-avoidance mechanism in R13 can read it), (c) refused-run records preserve `target` (so the per-target rolling counters in R13 work), (d) the file is parseable line-by-line as JSONL even when concurrent writes happen (the lockfile R14 should make this a non-issue but the invariant is unstated). Without these checks, AC-15 verifies presence-of-fields but not the corpus integrity invariants the goal Outcome relies on.
findings.claim: Goal-coverage gap — the goal Outcome names Phase 3 corpus-mining as a success surface, but no AC verifies the corpus integrity invariants (id uniqueness, operator preservation on declined records, target preservation on refused records, line-parseability under concurrency). A run record where `id` collides with a prior record, or where `winner_operator` is dropped on a declined record, would still pass AC-15 (presence-of-fields) while breaking the Phase 3 mining the corpus exists to enable.
findings.proposed_change: Extend AC-15 with explicit corpus-integrity sub-clauses: '(a) Across all records in `admin/optimize-runs.jsonl`, the `id` field is unique (no two records share the same `id`); (b) records with `merge_decision: "closed-without-merge"` have a non-null `winner_operator`; (c) records with `merge_decision: "null-failed-run"` have a non-null `target` AND a non-null `refuse_reason`; (d) the file is valid JSONL — every line parses as JSON in isolation, no partial writes.' These four invariants are what Phase 3 mining reads; verifying them in AC-15 closes the goal-coverage gap. A new R-level requirement is unnecessary — the goal-field plus extended AC-15 binds the skill to the corpus contract.
